precepts.text: Joshua shall stand before Eleazar the priest, who shall ask counsel for him after the judgment of Urim before the Lord.
precepts.point: Joshua likewise was to stand before Eleazar the priest, who shall ask counsel for him after the judgment of Urim before the Lord; the Most High gave revelation through it.

note.label: Exodus 28: Holy Garments for Glory and for Beauty

precepts.why:
Joshua likewise was to “stand before Eleazar the priest, who shall ask counsel for him after the judgment of Urim before the Lord: at his word shall they go out, and at his word they shall come in, both he, and all the children of Israel with him, even all the congregation.”

The Most High gave revelation through the Urim. The high priest carried the authority to seek counsel of the Most High, and His will was revealed to him; that is how the leader of the whole congregation knew when to go out and when to come in. That is what it means that Aaron bore “the judgment of the children of Israel upon his heart before the Lord continually.”

precepts.text: Let them marry to whom they think best, only within the tribe of their father, so the inheritance does not remove from tribe to tribe.
precepts.point: But what if a daughter who received the inheritance married into another tribe? You have to go precept upon precept: Numbers 36 takes up that very case with these same daughters. The chief fathers of Gilead brought it to Moses, and the word came back that the daughters of Zelophehad may marry to whom they think best, only to the family of the tribe of their father shall they marry.

note.label: Numbers 27: The Daughters of Zelophehad and the Ordination of Joshua

precepts.why:
The Lord set the order of inheritance for all Israel: to the daughter if there is no son, then to the brethren, then to the father's brethren, then to the next kinsman of his family. Every angle was covered so the inheritance stayed within the tribe. Israel always had questions, just as we do when we read, and the Lord put these statutes in place to answer them before they were asked.

But what if a daughter who received the inheritance married into another tribe? You have to go precept upon precept: Numbers 36 takes up that very case with these same daughters. The chief fathers of Gilead brought it to Moses, and the word came back: “This is the thing which the Lord doth command concerning the daughters of Zelophehad, saying, Let them marry to whom they think best; only to the family of the tribe of their father shall they marry.”

“So shall not the inheritance of the children of Israel remove from tribe to tribe: for every one of the children of Israel shall keep himself to the inheritance of the tribe of his fathers.” Where an inheritance rode on the marriage, the woman married within her father's tribe.

precepts.text: Every daughter that possesses an inheritance shall be wife unto one of the family of the tribe of her father, that every man enjoy the inheritance of his fathers.
precepts.point: But what if a daughter who received the inheritance married into another tribe? You have to go precept upon precept: Numbers 36 takes up that very case with these same daughters. The chief fathers of Gilead brought it to Moses, and the word came back that the daughters of Zelophehad may marry to whom they think best, only to the family of the tribe of their father shall they marry.

note.label: Numbers 27: The Daughters of Zelophehad and the Ordination of Joshua

precepts.why:
The statute of judgment in Numbers 27 passed the inheritance to the daughter, and Numbers 36 settles whom that daughter marries. “And every daughter, that possesseth an inheritance in any tribe of the children of Israel, shall be wife unto one of the family of the tribe of her father, that the children of Israel may enjoy every man the inheritance of his fathers.”

“Neither shall the inheritance remove from one tribe to another tribe; but every one of the tribes of the children of Israel shall keep himself to his own inheritance.” This is not saying no one ever married from Judah to Benjamin or Levi to Ephraim; it is showing that where an inheritance rode on the marriage, the woman married within her father's tribe, that every man enjoy the inheritance of his fathers.

precepts.text: The daughters of Zelophehad were married unto their father's brothers' sons, and the inheritance remained in the tribe of the family of their father.
precepts.point: But what if a daughter who received the inheritance married into another tribe? You have to go precept upon precept: Numbers 36 takes up that very case with these same daughters. The chief fathers of Gilead brought it to Moses, and the word came back that the daughters of Zelophehad may marry to whom they think best, only to the family of the tribe of their father shall they marry.

note.label: Numbers 27: The Daughters of Zelophehad and the Ordination of Joshua

precepts.why:
The daughters whose case brought this statute of judgment did as it was commanded. “Even as the Lord commanded Moses, so did the daughters of Zelophehad: For Mahlah, Tirzah, and Hoglah, and Milcah, and Noah, the daughters of Zelophehad, were married unto their father’s brothers’ sons.”

“And they were married into the families of the sons of Manasseh the son of Joseph, and their inheritance remained in the tribe of the family of their father.” The inheritance that passed to them under Numbers 27 stayed in Manasseh, because they married their father's brothers' sons.

precepts.text: Chiefly take a wife of the seed of thy fathers; our fathers from the beginning all married wives of their own kindred, and were blessed in their children.
precepts.point: It also goes into marriage in the nation as a whole: there was never a case where an inheritance in Israel passed to an Edomite, an Ammonite, or a Moabite. The fathers from the beginning took wives of their own kindred, and interracial marriage is not of the scriptures.

note.label: Numbers 27: The Daughters of Zelophehad and the Ordination of Joshua

precepts.why:
The order of inheritance also goes into marriage in the nation as a whole: there was never a case where an inheritance in Israel passed to an Edomite, an Ammonite, or a Moabite.

“Beware of all whoredom, my son, and chiefly take a wife of the seed of thy fathers, and take not a strange woman to wife, which is not of thy father’s tribe: for we are the children of the prophets, Noe, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: remember, my son, that our fathers from the beginning, even that they all married wives of their own kindred, and were blessed in their children, and their seed shall inherit the land.”

Chiefly take a wife of the seed of thy fathers; our fathers from the beginning all married wives of their own kindred, and were blessed in their children, and their seed shall inherit the land. Interracial marriage is not of the scriptures.

precepts.text: The commandment was to speak unto the rock; Moses smote it twice, and because they believed not, to sanctify the Lord in the eyes of Israel, they did not bring the congregation into the land.
precepts.point: The reason is written: Moses rebelled against the commandment of the Most High in the desert of Zin at the water of Meribah. The Lord gave a specific commandment to speak unto the rock before their eyes, and Moses instead smote the rock twice; the water still came out abundantly, but Moses and Aaron did not sanctify the Lord in the eyes of the children of Israel, and for that neither of them brought the congregation into the land.

note.label: Numbers 27: The Daughters of Zelophehad and the Ordination of Joshua

precepts.why:
Moses would see the land from mount Abarim but not enter it, and be gathered unto his people as Aaron was, “For ye rebelled against my commandment in the desert of Zin, in the strife of the congregation, to sanctify me at the water before their eyes.” Here is that rebellion.

The Lord gave a specific commandment: “Take the rod, and gather thou the assembly together, thou, and Aaron thy brother, and speak ye unto the rock before their eyes; and it shall give forth his water.” Speak unto the rock. Instead Moses said, “Hear now, ye rebels; must we fetch you water out of this rock? And Moses lifted up his hand, and with his rod he smote the rock twice: and the water came out abundantly, and the congregation drank, and their beasts also.”

The water still came out abundantly, but the commandment was broken. “And the Lord spake unto Moses and Aaron, Because ye believed me not, to sanctify me in the eyes of the children of Israel, therefore ye shall not bring this congregation into the land which I have given them.” Moses and Aaron did not sanctify the Lord in the eyes of the children of Israel, and for that neither of them brought the congregation into the land.

precepts.text: Children are their oppressors, and women rule over them; that condition is a mark of a people gone astray, not the order of the Most High.
precepts.point: A sister helping to build up other sisters new in the congregation is right, and the sisters bless the nation with real talents, raising the children in the commandments, and the aged women teaching the young women. But teaching and leading the nation is not the place the Most High set for her.

note.label: Numbers 27: The Daughters of Zelophehad and the Ordination of Joshua

precepts.why:
Moses asked the Lord to “set a man over the congregation”, a man to go out and come in before them, that the congregation “be not as sheep which have no shepherd.” He asked for a man because the leadership of the nation belongs to men.

“As for my people, children are their oppressors, and women rule over them. O my people, they which lead thee cause thee to err, and destroy the way of thy paths.” Women ruling over the people is a mark of a people gone astray, not the order of the Most High; they which lead in that condition cause the people to err.

The woman was made to be an help meet unto the man, not to rule over him; she is the weaker vessel, and the congregation is not set up for her to lead it.

note.label: Numbers 27: The Daughters of Zelophehad and the Ordination of Joshua

The reason is from the beginning: “For Adam was first formed, then Eve. And Adam was not deceived, but the woman being deceived was in the transgression.” The woman was made to be an help meet unto the man, not to rule over him; she is the weaker vessel.

A sister helping to build up other sisters new in the congregation is right, but teaching and leading the nation is not the place the Most High set for her.

precepts.text: The daughters of Zelophehad pleaded that their father died in his own sin with no son, and asked why his name should be done away from among his family.
precepts.point: Their concern is real: if the daughters marry men of another tribe, their father's inheritance passes with them to the husband's tribe, and at the jubilee it is fixed to that tribe, so the tribe of Manasseh loses that land forever.

note.label: Numbers 36: The Inheritance of the Daughters of Zelophehad

precepts.why:
The chief fathers of Gilead, of the tribe of Manasseh, bring an issue rising out of what was already ruled in Numbers 27. Zelophehad died in the wilderness with no sons, and his daughters had pleaded: “Our father died in the wilderness, and he was not in the company of them that gathered themselves together against the Lord in the company of Korah; but died in his own sin, and had no sons.”

“Why should the name of our father be done away from among his family, because he hath no son? Give unto us therefore a possession among the brethren of our father.” That plea is where the inheritance of Zelophehad’s daughters came from, and it is the inheritance the fathers of Gilead now fear to lose to another tribe.

precepts.text: The Lord ruled the daughters spoke right: if a man die and have no son, his inheritance passes to his daughter; that ruling set up the question of Numbers 36.
precepts.point: Their concern is real: if the daughters marry men of another tribe, their father's inheritance passes with them to the husband's tribe, and at the jubilee it is fixed to that tribe, so the tribe of Manasseh loses that land forever.

note.label: Numbers 36: The Inheritance of the Daughters of Zelophehad

precepts.why:
“And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying, The daughters of Zelophehad speak right: thou shalt surely give them a possession of an inheritance among their father’s brethren; and thou shalt cause the inheritance of their father to pass unto them.” The Lord ruled that Zelophehad’s inheritance pass to his daughters, and made it law: “If a man die, and have no son, then ye shall cause his inheritance to pass unto his daughter.”

That ruling set up the question of Numbers 36. The concern of the chief fathers is real: if the daughters marry men of another tribe, their father’s inheritance passes with them to the husband’s tribe, and at the jubile it is fixed to that tribe, so the tribe of Manasseh loses that land forever.

precepts.text: Moses asked the Lord to set a man over the congregation to lead them out and bring them in, that Israel be not as sheep without a shepherd.
precepts.point: Why was Joshua the one anointed? When the Lord told Moses he would see the land but not enter it, Moses did not argue or justify himself. His humble response was to ask the Lord to set a man over the congregation, that the congregation of the Lord be not as sheep which have no shepherd. Moses brought no candidates; he let the Lord pick, and the Lord picked the young man who had cleaved to him: promotion comes from the Lord, and he selects the leaders over his people.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

precepts.why:
Why was Joshua the one anointed? When the Lord told Moses he would see the land but not enter it, Moses did not argue or justify himself. His humble response was this: “Let the Lord, the God of the spirits of all flesh, set a man over the congregation, Which may go out before them, and which may go in before them, and which may lead them out, and which may bring them in; that the congregation of the Lord be not as sheep which have no shepherd.”

Moses asked the Lord to set a man over the congregation to lead them out and bring them in, that Israel be not as sheep without a shepherd. He brought no candidates; he let the Lord pick.

And he said set a man over the congregation, not a woman, because women were never ordained to lead the children of Israel; that does not fit the divine order of the Most High.

precepts.text: The Lord said, Take thee Joshua the son of Nun, a man in whom is the spirit; Moses laid his hand on him, set him before Eleazar and the congregation, and put some of his honour upon him so the people would give Joshua the same respect and be obedient.
precepts.point: Why was Joshua the one anointed? When the Lord told Moses he would see the land but not enter it, Moses did not argue or justify himself. His humble response was to ask the Lord to set a man over the congregation, that the congregation of the Lord be not as sheep which have no shepherd. Moses brought no candidates; he let the Lord pick, and the Lord picked the young man who had cleaved to him: promotion comes from the Lord, and he selects the leaders over his people.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

precepts.why:
The Lord picked: “Take thee Joshua the son of Nun, a man in whom is the spirit, and lay thine hand upon him”. The Lord picked the young man who had cleaved to Moses, a man in whom is the spirit. Promotion comes from the Lord, and he selects the leaders over his people.

“And set him before Eleazar the priest, and before all the congregation; and give him a charge in their sight. And thou shalt put some of thine honour upon him, that all the congregation of the children of Israel may be obedient.” Moses laid his hand on him, set him before Eleazar and the congregation, and put some of his honour upon him so the people would give Joshua the same respect they gave Moses, and be obedient. That is how “Moses my servant is dead; now therefore arise” comes to Joshua and no one else.

precepts.text: Moses asked the Lord to set a man over the congregation, a man to go out before them and bring them in, that the congregation of the Lord be not as sheep which have no shepherd.
precepts.point: Verse 9 proves it: my heart is toward the governors of Israel, the leaders who offered themselves willingly among the people. Her heart was with the men who led; she was not ruling over them.

note.label: Judges 5: The Song of Deborah and Barak: A Willing People

precepts.why:
This passage is for all the closet feminists who think Deborah justifies women leading men. Look at the order the Most High set. Moses asked, “Let the Lord, the God of the spirits of all flesh, set a man over the congregation, Which may go out before them, and which may go in before them, and which may lead them out, and which may bring them in; that the congregation of the Lord be not as sheep which have no shepherd.”

A man goes out before the congregation and brings them in. Deborah did not lead men into any kind of war; she did not put on body armor and a breastplate, rise up on a horse, and lead the charge. She “arose a mother in Israel”, the motivating factor to men that were shaky and fearful during that time, a guiding light. Verse 9 proves it: “My heart is toward the governors of Israel, that offered themselves willingly among the people.” Her heart was with the men who led; she was not ruling over them.

precepts.text: The Lord answered in total agreement with what Moses spoke: take thee Joshua the son of Nun, a man in whom is the spirit; the Lord set a man over the congregation.
precepts.point: Verse 9 proves it: my heart is toward the governors of Israel, the leaders who offered themselves willingly among the people. Her heart was with the men who led; she was not ruling over them.

note.label: Judges 5: The Song of Deborah and Barak: A Willing People

precepts.why:
The Lord answered Moses in total agreement with what he spoke: “Take thee Joshua the son of Nun, a man in whom is the spirit, and lay thine hand upon him.” Moses asked for a man over the congregation, and the Lord set a man.

That is the pattern Deborah fits inside, not outside. She was a mother in Israel whose heart was “toward the governors of Israel”, the men who “offered themselves willingly among the people.” The men governed and went out before the people; she did not usurp that.

precepts.text: In the context of selecting a leader over the congregation, the Most High is called the God of the spirits of all flesh; the selection is always spiritual.
precepts.point: This still happens today: brothers will look at a group and assume the biggest one must be the leader, not knowing that brother might be the soldier while the leader is the slim one beside him.

note.label: 1 Samuel 16: The Lord Looketh on the Heart

precepts.why:
“Let the Lord, the God of the spirits of all flesh, set a man over the congregation, Which may go out before them, and which may go in before them, and which may lead them out, and which may bring them in; that the congregation of the Lord be not as sheep which have no shepherd.”

In the context of selecting a leader over the congregation, the Most High is called the God of the spirits of all flesh. The selection is always spiritual. So when Samuel came to anoint a king among Jesse’s sons, the Lord did not choose by countenance or stature; he looked on the heart.

points: The Lord answered: take thee Joshua the son of Nun, a man in whom is the spirit, and lay thine hand upon him.

note.label: Numbers 27: The Daughters of Zelophehad and the Ordination of Joshua

points: Joshua was set before Eleazar the priest and before all the congregation and given his charge in their sight, and some of Moses' honour was put upon him, so all Israel could see with their own eyes the man the Most High ordained to lead the nation after the death of Moses.

note.label: Numbers 27: The Daughters of Zelophehad and the Ordination of Joshua

points: Joshua was to stand before Eleazar the priest, who would ask counsel for him after the judgment of Urim before the Lord; at his word they would go out and come in, he and all the children of Israel with him.

note.label: Numbers 27: The Daughters of Zelophehad and the Ordination of Joshua

points: Moses did as the Lord commanded him: he took Joshua, set him before Eleazar the priest and all the congregation, laid his hands upon him, and gave him a charge, as the Lord commanded by the hand of Moses.
